## Module overview

This is the creative part of CREATE. You write your own next experiment to follow the ones in the paper — one that fills a gap or extends the paper. You discuss proposals with peers, review them as a grant panel, and submit a revised proposal.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- Discuss your proposed studies with peers.
- Summarize the implications of your proposed work.
- Identify the strengths and weaknesses of your proposal.
- Incorporate feedback to submit a revised grant proposal.

## Proposal outline

<details><summary>Hint: Strong proposals</summary>
State a testable question, a hypothesis, the experiment you would run, and the result that would support or refute your hypothesis.
</details>

Use these headings: **Gap**, **Hypothesis**, **Aims/Experiments**, **Controls and readouts**, **Expected results**, **Implications**, **Limitations**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m7q1", "Which makes the best next experiment?", ["One that repeats Figure 1", "One that tests a specific hypothesis addressing a gap", "One with no controls", "One unrelated to the paper"], 1, "Aim at a clear gap with a testable hypothesis.")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
notes("m7-draft", "Gap, hypothesis, experiment, controls, expected results.")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
notes("m7-feedback", "Strengths, weaknesses, and how you will revise.")
```

## Revised proposal notes

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
notes("m7-revised", "Record your revisions.")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m7q2", "A strong follow-up proposal should…", ["Repeat the paper exactly", "Fill a gap or extend the findings with a testable question, controls and a readout", "Avoid stating a hypothesis", "Skip peer feedback"], 1, "Good proposals are testable and address a gap.")
```

::: {.takeaways}
### Key takeaways
- Proposals state a question, hypothesis, controls and readout.
- Peer feedback helps you find strengths and weaknesses to revise.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Article: Huang et al. (2023), *Delftia tsuruhatensis* TC1 symbiont suppresses malaria transmission by anopheline mosquitoes, *Science*. <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf8141>
:::
